matches.note: R2 describes the identical defect: pending change applied onto a CANCELLED row because cancellation never voids pending changes and applyPendingChanges never checks status.
R9 identifies the missing payment_behavior and resulting 'incomplete' subscription, but describes the consequence as a CHECK-violation rollback with no local row, not an unpaid tier being granted.
R2 explicitly states both getCoachSubscriptionTier and resolvePlayerTierKey read tier with no status check, granting paid entitlements on non-live rows.
R1 states downgrades only write a local change row and applyPendingChanges never calls Stripe, so the old higher price keeps billing — same defect and consequence.
No reported finding says changeCoachTier/changePlayerTier lack a status check; R10 concerns the cancelAtPeriodEnd flag, not PAST_DUE/CANCELLED status.
R7 covers the local-only grace expiry with Stripe left billing; R5 covers subscribeCoach/subscribePlayer passing the guard and creating a second live Stripe subscription.
R3 states pastDueSince is never nulled on recovery so a later failure gets zero grace — same mechanism and consequence.

R9 covers unmapped statuses violating chk_pcs_status/chk_pps_status and the webhook rollback/retry loop; R6 covers the absent event-ordering guard; only the missing invoice.paid handler fragment is uncovered.
No reported finding describes the load-before-Stripe/save-after lost update or the missing @Version field.
R4 identifies the customer+price idempotency key replaying a stale creation response within 24h, including the resubscribe case, plus the cross-player collision.

R10 touches the proration/cancel-at-period-end interaction in change-tier but inverts the scenario and consequence (claims proration is charged on a dying subscription rather than deferred and never collected).
R6 concerns ordering of delivered events, not the subscribe race where an event finds no row, is suppressed by the grace window, and is acknowledged and lost.

R8 identifies the raw-cased tier persisted after Stripe was charged with the same rollback-after-charge consequence, attributing it to the tier CHECK rather than enum valueOf and omitting the player 'pro' quota-fallback fragment.
